To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose novel metaphors to increase user's safety and enjoyment in large VEs, (2) we provide a comprehensive comparison of three new techniques with traditional controller-based interfaces in a controlled user study, and (3) we conclude that the new techniques can be used as a complement to existing interfaces to improve safety, walking distance, and enjoyment.

(i) we propose a new metaphor for locomotion in VR, based on the idea of a bird that guides the user through a virtual space, (ii) this metaphor is very intuitive and enjoyable, (iii) it is very safe and (iv) it is more efficient than traditional controller-based techniques.
the three new locomotion techniques we introduce provide a safer and more enjoyable interaction paradigm compared to the standard wand controller.

the design of new locomotion paradigms that are safe, enjoyable and increase physical walking.
improving the safety, realism and fun of locomotion in immersive virtual reality.

the design of novel locomotion techniques to safely navigate large virtual environments in restricted physical workspaces, while increasing the amount of real-world walking and providing a more enjoyable experience.
